To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
size-frequency distributions of fossil assemblages are a useful tool in paleoecological analysis.

the size-frequency distributions of parautochthonic death assemblages are useful in paleoecological analysis and that changes in the size-frequency distribution can be used to infer changes in the community structure of the living assemblages from which the parautochthonus death assemblages were derived.

the size-frequency distribution and the energy flow of size classes in a death assemblage can be applied to paleoecological analysis and that the size-frequency distributions of species and of the assemblages are persistent features of the community structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of size-frequency distributions in paleoecological analysis and the application of energy flow models to paleocommunity structure.
the application of the energy flow approach to paleoecology.
the use of the size-frequency distributions in paleoecological studies and the application of energy flow in the analysis of paleoecological data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the size-frequency distribution and its associated parameters are a valuable tool in the analysis of fossil assemblages.

a change in assemblages from chemoautotrophy to filter-feeding, and the increase in assemblage size, are both indicative of a change in food supply and that the size-frequency distribution is a useful tool in paleoecological analysis.
the size-frequency distribution is a useful tool for paleoecological research.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the size-frequency distribution and the energy flow associated with it are valuable parameters for paleoecologic studies.
the size-frequency distribution and the associated measures of energy flow are valuable tools in the analysis of paleoecological change.
the size-frequency distribution provides a valuable tool for analyzing the fossil record, especially when combined with the energy flow model.
The main takeaway from our work is that

paleoecologists should not be content with the use of size frequency distributions to describe assemblage structure but should use the distribution to evaluate the structure of energy flow through size classes in assemblages and the community.

size is a fundamental feature of community structure that can be measured from the fossil record, and that the distribution of energy flux amongst size classes can be used to identify the effects of environmental change on the structure of the community.

the size-frequency distribution is an important parameter in paleoecological analysis because it is a temporally persistent parameter that reflects changes in community structure, and that the size-frequency distributions of assemblages are more informative than the size-frequency distributions obtained for individual species.
